title: Utabridge
subtitle: Near-production prototype for language-assisted music discovery
summary: Utabridge was a browser-extension-driven product prototype for helping listeners understand Japanese music more easily. It paired a Spring Boot backend with a React extension experience and reached a near-production stage, but was not publicly launched.
problem: Japanese songs often require jumping between music platforms, lyrics sites, translations, and language references. The experience is fragmented for listeners who want both the song and its meaning in context.
solution: Built a product prototype around a browser extension interface backed by a Spring Boot API, with the goal of bridging song context, lyrics, and language support directly into the listening flow.
impact: Reached a near-production prototype stage
Explored a real product workflow around browser extensions, backend APIs, and user-facing language tooling
Helped clarify the complexity of shipping browser-extension products beyond the core implementation

title: Aarohan Download Fix Extension
subtitle: Browser extension to fix download issues in the Aarohan portal
summary: A practical browser extension built to fix download issues in the Aarohan portal. The project focused on solving a specific real-world annoyance with a lightweight extension rather than building a large standalone app.
problem: The Aarohan portal had a broken or inconvenient download flow that made accessing files more painful than it needed to be.
solution: Built a browser extension using WXT and React to improve the download behavior and smooth out the user flow.
impact: Solved a concrete usability issue with a small targeted tool
Used a modern browser extension stack with WXT and React
Demonstrated practical problem-solving outside of traditional CRUD app projects

title: Dock Command Authority
subtitle: Distributed locking for safe multi-user drone command control
summary: Designed and implemented Redis-based command authority controls for DJI Dock operations to ensure only one user could actively control a drone during livestream sessions.
problem: Multiple users could view drone livestreams, but command control needed to be exclusive. Without explicit authority management, overlapping user actions could create conflicting drone commands and unsafe operational behavior.
solution: Implemented a Redis-backed distributed locking mechanism to grant exclusive command authority to one active controller while allowing other users to remain viewers.
impact: Prevented conflicting drone commands during multi-user sessions
Enabled safer remote drone operations
Introduced a clear authority model for livestream-based control flows

title: MQTT Event Bus
subtitle: Command response routing layer for DJI Dock MQTT workflows
summary: Built an event bus abstraction over MQTT command handling to route responses correctly despite the underlying MQTT client allowing only a single callback handler per topic.
problem: The MQTT client library allowed only one handler for a topic, which created a bottleneck for command-response workflows. Different dock commands could interfere with each other, causing incorrect pending states and unreliable command feedback.
solution: Designed an internal event bus that multiplexed topic callbacks and routed command responses back to the correct waiting workflow.
impact: Eliminated incorrect or stuck command states
Allowed multiple dock command workflows to safely share MQTT topics
Improved reliability of remote command execution and response tracking

title: Map Rendering Optimization
subtitle: Reduced geospatial layer loading from minutes to seconds
summary: Optimized a slow geospatial map rendering workflow by parallelizing vector contour fetches and removing main-thread blocking behavior.
problem: Rendering map layers required thousands of sequential vector contour requests, causing load times of more than five minutes and blocking the user interface.
solution: Parallelized the vector contour fetching workflow and reworked the loading behavior so the map could become usable much faster.
impact: Reduced map loading time from 5+ minutes to roughly 5–10 seconds
Improved rendering performance by around 50x
Removed major UI blocking during heavy geospatial layer loading

title: Geospatial ML Annotation Tooling
subtitle: Self-serve raster annotation workflow for object detection models
summary: Built tooling that allowed customers to annotate raster data and trigger geospatial ML workflows for object detection use cases.
problem: Model customization requests required manual annotation and engineering involvement, creating a slow repetitive workflow that could take weeks before customers saw usable results.
solution: Built a Mapbox/GeoJSON-based annotation interface and connected it to a pipeline that could fine-tune object detection models and run inference on customer-provided data.
impact: Reduced a manual model request workflow from around a month to a much shorter self-serve process
Enabled customers to annotate rasters and define classes themselves
Reduced repetitive internal effort for geospatial ML customization requests

title: Chargebee Billing Integration
subtitle: Self-serve subscription and payment workflows for enterprise SaaS
summary: Integrated Chargebee to support self-serve subscriptions, payments, webhooks, and internal custom-plan management.
problem: Subscription and billing workflows depended heavily on manual setup. Custom plans required internal database changes or migration-style interventions, which made billing operations slow and error-prone.
solution: Integrated Chargebee billing flows, handled webhook-driven subscription state changes, and built internal tooling for managing custom plans without direct database edits.
impact: Enabled self-serve subscription and payment workflows
Reduced manual billing operations
Removed the need for direct database edits for custom plan setup

title: Custom Authentication System
subtitle: JWT-based login flow to remove enterprise Google URL dependency
summary: Implemented a custom authentication flow with self-issued JWTs and phone/email login support to reduce onboarding friction for enterprise users.
problem: The existing authentication flow depended on enterprise Google URL behavior and firewall whitelisting, which created onboarding friction for some users.
solution: Introduced a custom JWT-based authentication layer with phone and email login support, reducing dependency on enterprise-specific Google access flows.
impact: Reduced onboarding friction for enterprise users
Removed firewall whitelisting steps tied to the previous auth flow
Expanded supported login options with phone and email authentication

title: GraphQL to REST Migration
subtitle: Migrated backend APIs from GraphQL to Django REST Framework
summary: Migrated GraphQL APIs to Django REST Framework to improve maintainability, reduce dependency risk, and simplify backend development workflows.
problem: The existing GraphQL layer introduced maintenance overhead and dependency risk, especially around Graphene and related ecosystem constraints.
solution: Rebuilt key API surfaces using Django REST Framework, replacing GraphQL endpoints with typed REST API implementations.
impact: Improved backend maintainability
Reduced dependency risk around GraphQL tooling
Simplified API development and debugging workflows

title: CardGen
subtitle: Early full-stack design tool built during internship
summary: An early Canva-like card design tool built during an internship. It is kept as an archived project because it reflects older experience and is not representative of current engineering ability.
problem: Users needed a lightweight interface for creating simple card-style designs.
solution: Built a web-based design tool with a Svelte frontend and Firebase backend during an internship project.
impact: Delivered an early full-stack application as part of internship work
Practiced product UI design, frontend implementation, and Firebase-backed persistence
